doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Jazz-freak high school years and Berklee
summary: He heard great players at Blues Alley while in Virginia, struggled with his school band, then found like-minded players at Berklee.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You had a pretty good experience in high school and so forth with jazz?

Well I was a jazz freak and I converted a few of my closest friends to being jazz freaks, and some of them had driver’s licenses before I did, so I was able to cajole them into driving into Washington D.C. — I grew up in Virginia. And we’d go to Blues Alley. And at Blues Alley I heard Earl Hines and Clark Terry and Lockjaw Davis and Dizzy Gillespie, Bobby Hackett, Zoot Sims — a lot of great, great musicians. And I would sit right in front with a glass of water, and just take a lesson. It was great. I did that as often as I could. But it was hard because I didn’t drive. And later I got a driver’s license and I was able to go in myself. But those years in high school were a little tough in a way because it was frustrating. I tried to have a band, I put a little group together, and I was rehearsing it, and it’s hard — we couldn’t get any work, we couldn’t get guys to rehearse, I could never get the bass player to bring his bow because I was always writing thing where I wanted arco bass, and the bass player never wanted to bring the bow. It was a © Hamilton Fillius Archive -3-
little bit of a struggle. So when I finally got to college, Berklee College of Music in Boston, suddenly I was surrounded with people that wanted to do what I was trying to do.
They had the same passion as you perhaps.

Yeah, it’s like let’s rehearse, let’s play jam sessions with the right tunes, we used to rehearse all the time, let’s get together this afternoon, let’s see how slow we can play, let’s see how fast we can play, let’s do duets, let’s do just tenor and drums. You know, trying every possible thing. It was really great, a great time.
